Simon — thanks for the clear summary. High level guidance first, then a proposed next-step checklist.

1) Latency vs. batching/caching
- Batching: increases throughput and lowers per-token cost but adds queuing latency. For strict P95 <150ms with 60–120 token requests, continuous batching is risky unless you can accept burst-based micro-batching with very short max-wait (1–3ms) and strong autoscale. We generally see micro-batches of 2–4 reduce cost a little but not enough to justify added latency for your SLO.
- Prefix/KV caching: this is your best lever. If a meaningful portion of the prompt is repetitive (system prompts, templates, or shared context), KV caching cuts per-request compute dramatically without adding latency. Cache hit complexity: ensure stable session keys and warm-up for cold sessions.

2) Quantization recommendations (accuracy vs. latency/cost)
- Baseline: FP16 on our hosted nodes gives the best fidelity.
- Int8 (AMP/ONNX-style dynamic quant) on Ampere-class GPUs is a low-risk step: ~10–25% cost improvement with negligible AUC impact for most Llama2 variants. Good for early production.
- 4-bit (QLoRA / group-wise) yields larger savings (2–4x lower memory footprint) but is model- and prompt-sensitive; expect occasional tail-case quality regressions. If you pursue 4-bit: run an eval set we can provide and a short 2-week canary run.
- Practical note: 4-bit variants sometimes require runtime kernel fallback for certain attention kernels; that can slightly increase P95 if not pinned to an optimized runtime. Redwood Optimize can recommend kernel profiles and a quantization plan.

3) Packaging and pricing path
- Pilot (4–6 weeks): Hosted credits + Optimize toolkit audit. We typically structure this as $X in hosted credits + up to 2 weeks of free canary monitoring and a quantization evaluation report.
- Pre-prod: Small Dedicated pool (1–2 nodes) with autoscale headroom; commit to a monthly minimum for predictable pricing and reduced per-token rates.
- Production: Tiered commit with volume bands and Optimize credits applied to caching/batching advisory services. We can include a 10% pilot-to-production migration credit if you commit within 60 days.

4) Ops considerations
- Warm VMs and pre-warmed KV cache for the first 1k users in a rollout window.
- Canary run should measure AUC drift, P95 latency, and cold-start tail latencies. Redwood Console will export traces and Token-level cost breakdowns.

Attachments & links: I'm attaching a short deck that sketches the Dedicated vs Hosted cost model and a sample inference config we use for low-latency customers. Also linking a HubSpot deal and the evaluation checklist.
